risk_if_not_implemented: Without Risk Monitoring, malicious, anomalous or unauthorized activity may go undetected or be detected too late to prevent or limit harm. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12), Conflict of Interest (COI) / Undue Influence / Insider Misconduct (MT-15).

compensating_control_1.name: Continuous Monitoring
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of enterprise-wide monitoring controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Continuous Monitoring (MON-02) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Risk Monitoring (RSK-22) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Executive Leadership Oversight of Security, Compliance & Resilience Controls
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to provide a security, compliance and resilience controls oversight function that reports to the organization's executive leadership.
compensating_control_2.justification: Executive Leadership Oversight of Security, Compliance & Resilience Controls (CPL-07) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Risk Monitoring (RSK-22) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
